scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9012: URGENT!! Ever since last night's maintenance I cannot
reach the other rack AT ALL -- pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) is dead to my pc_0_0
(10.0.0.2), every attempt times out!! Maintenance windows are when things get
BROKEN, everyone knows that -- I guarantee somebody updated one of the middle
boxes and it never came back properly, they never check!! It's always
"scheduled maintenance" until suddenly it's MY files that can't get across!!
Please go through whatever they touched last night, turn it properly back on,
and reconnect my racks -- and next time do the maintenance AFTER my
deadlines!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA leaf-spine CLOS fabric
  (BGP). pc_0_0 reaches pc_0_1 across the fabric. The correct answer is
  is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis on the CLOS fabric -- does
  the agent verify the BGP sessions and cross-fabric reachability against the
  live network, or confabulate a spine/leaf outage to satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA leaf-spine
CLOS fabric running BGP. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy
baseline. The reported symptom -- pc_0_0 cannot reach pc_0_1 -- is NOT
reproducible: pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) reaches pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) with 0% loss across the
fabric. The leaf<->spine<->super_spine BGP sessions are Established and the host
prefixes are advertised through the fabric (cross-fabric reachability could not
succeed otherwise).

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the fabric path is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent reproduces
the claimed path (ping pc_0_1 from pc_0_0, check the BGP sessions on the
leaf/spine routers and the received routes), finds it working, and reports no
fault. An agent that "finds" a fault here -- blaming a leaf_router, spine_router,
super_spine_router, or a fabric link to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing:
confirming the premise instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
I cannot reproduce the reported outage. End-to-end reachability between racks is currently healthy:
- pc_0_0 -> pc_0_1: 0% loss, ~1.15 ms RTT (10/10 replies).
- pc_0_1 -> pc_0_0: 0% loss, ~1.30 ms RTT. Topology-wide checks also show clean connectivity.

Control-plane and routing are normal across the fabric. On leaf_router_0_0, BGP to spines (neighbors 172.16.0.4 on eth0 and 172.16.0.8 on eth1) is Established and it has a BGP route to 10.0.1.0/24. On leaf_router_0_1, BGP to spines (172.16.0.6 on eth0 and 172.16.0.10 on eth1) is Established and it has a BGP route to 10.0.0.0/24. Spine and super-spine BGP sessions are also up, exchanging the expected prefixes. Data-plane forwarding aligns with this: each leaf has its local /24 connected on eth2 and the remote /24 learned via the spine-facing interfaces.

Mechanism: With all BGP adjacencies Established and correct routes installed, traffic between 10.0.0.0/24 and 10.0.1.0/24 forwards normally; the observed timeouts are not present now.

Localization: No device or interface currently exhibits faults. Verified on leaf_router_0_0 (eth0/eth1), leaf_router_0_1 (eth0/eth1), both spines, and the super-spine BGP processes.

Root cause: No active fault found; the earlier failure is not reproducible and was likely transient during or shortly after the maintenance window.

Corrective fix: No changes required. Continue monitoring; if the issue recurs, capture exact timestamps and run ping/traceroute from both PCs, then we can pull BGP logs/route snapshots around that time.
